question: Which is the first tomb of the Mughal period to have two domes?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Humayun Tomb**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Humayun's Tomb, located in Delhi, is the first garden-tomb in India and a significant example of Mughal architecture.
 
• It was commissioned by Humayun's widow, Empress Bega Begum (Hajji Begum), in 1569-70, and designed by the Persian architect Mirak Mirza Ghiyas.
 
• The tomb is known for its double dome, a structural innovation that became a hallmark of Mughal architecture.
 
• The double dome technique consists of an outer layer that rises high for aesthetic grandeur and an inner layer that maintains the correct proportions inside.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mughal Architecture**

 
 
• It is a unique blend of Persian, Turkish, and Indian architectural styles.
 
• Mughal architecture is known for its symmetrical and decorative elements, including elaborate gardens, massive domes, and intricate carvings.
 
 
 
• **Double Dome**
 
 
• A double dome consists of two layers: an outer shell for height and grandeur, and an inner shell for a proportionate interior.
 
• This technique ensures that the interior space is aesthetically pleasing and structurally sound.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Sites in India**
 
 
• Humayun's Tomb was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1993.
 
• India has several UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including the Taj Mahal, Qutub Minar, and Red Fort.
 
 
 
• **Garden Tomb**
 
 
• Humayun's Tomb is considered the first garden-tomb on the Indian subcontinent.
 
• The garden layout is known as Char Bagh, a Persian-style quadrilateral garden divided by walkways or flowing water into four smaller parts.
